title: Roles & User Management
description: The role/user administration surface: the Roles catalog and the AppUsers directory, plus the role/user admin pages and the permission model (role→table→field CRUD, per-role WHERE policies, role-specific schemas, derived RLS). Turn it OFF and an admin temporarily loses the management tools — a quick way to see the simpler app a non-admin sees. The underlying RLS keeps enforcing in Postgres regardless; this only hides the management UI.

title: Assistant & Cost Analytics
description: The portal assistant (the chat-agent state machine) plus its cost/usage telemetry: the AI model catalog (AiModels), the versioned model price book (ModelPricingVersions), and per-turn AssistantTurns rows whose token costs roll up to accounts and records. Turn it off to hide the assistant analytics surface; the assistant route still functions.

title: Citations & Contests
description: Core package: citations, hearings, payments, license points.

title: Core Platform
description: Cross-cutting platform machinery shared by all packages: the rulebook-driven permission model, role-specific schemas, the enforced CRUD API, row-level security, the generic state-machine backbone, the work queue, and dev-ops/build tooling.

title: Platform Meta & Knowledge Base
description: The self-describing meta layer you usually keep hidden: the feature catalog and statuses, the table/field schema catalog, the custom API-endpoint registry, ERB versions, customizations, the glossary, and the business-rule library. Turn this off and the entire "how the platform describes itself" surface disappears, leaving just the working app.

title: State Machine Admin
description: The state-machine configuration surface: the StateMachines / MachineStates / StateTransitionRules / StateTransitions tables and the admin routes that view and edit them (machines, states, transition rules, transition log). Turn it off to hide the entire state-machine admin UI; the machines still drive entity lifecycles in Postgres.
